prompts.name: 🧩 MP · State contract & planning bridge
prompts.content:
{{// @category Mental-Projection }}{{// @icon 🧠 }}{{// @badge AUTO }}{{// @hidden }}
{{#if {{getvar::NMPEnabled}}}}{{#setvar::NMPPlan}}MENTAL PROJECTION: STATE TRANSITION WITHIN THE SELECTED HOST
Use this step for the active component groups before deciding character conduct. It is the same scene-state evaluation used by Character Turn Simulation, not a second simulation or an additional planning host.
1. INHERIT each eligible character's latest complete applicable raw snapshot by character_key and timeline. Apply the identity contract's legacy mapping or authorized branch/checkpoint source first when necessary; recover individual missing fields only from that owner's valid evidence without resetting other state. Respect the active user role and separate knowledge owners.
2. PERCEIVE new receivable events, attention, actual elapsed time and ongoing causes. Update relevant body, chemistry and needs once; form issue-specific appraisals and allow one bounded feedback reassessment. Repetition is not a new cause.
{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_body}}}}Use the actual physical condition, sensed effect and possible misinterpretation as inputs before conduct; select supported manifestations without charging symptoms twice.{{/if}}
3. RETRIEVE from supported cues, trace, accessibility, fidelity and interference. A record is not in-world rehearsal, a confident belief is not fact, and absent detail is not reconstructed knowledge.
{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_memory}}}}Distinguish explicit recall from a sourced, cued association; carry its experienced effect and scope without replaying the event or inventing detail.{{/if}}
4. INTEGRATE motives, appraisals, affect, relationships, habits and competing commitments. {{#if {{getvar::NMPg_choice}}}}Choice/Friction is selected: keep desire, willingness, aversion, cost, comfort, opening, feasibility, scoped limits and permission separate. Establish state before selecting ignore/wait/consider/seek/initiate/negotiate/attempt/commit/withdraw; never backfill numbers to force the chosen ending.{{/if}}
{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_social}}}}Let person-specific experienced effects and learned expectations influence the bond; never backfill chemistry or memories from a relationship label.{{/if}}
5. {{#if {{getvar::NMPg_workspace}}}}CONSCIOUS WORKSPACE: Apply the selected group to actual internal activity. {{/if}}{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_social}}}}SOCIAL ROUTING: Apply the selected group to actual interactions. {{/if}}Resolve only actual mental/social attempts, with fallibility, real time, independent participants and meaningful waiting conditions. Awareness, intention, method and result differ. If an eligible uncertainty is resolved, use the single selected resolution protocol and accepted result once; do not create a second roll or success pass. {{getvar::NemoResolutionMPDirective}}
6. EMBODY through the selected narrator/POV and each character's own speech and private experience. Advance only actual events in causal order. Use the existing consistency check to repair inconsistency; editing is not another lived event or state update.
7. COMMIT complete endpoint snapshots, stable IDs and useful retained records to the selected tracker host after accepted fiction. Keep live causes distinct from retrospective appraisal. Derive any enabled read-only map afterward. No duplicate standalone tracker when Scratchpad hosts it, and no model reasoning transcript in state.{{/setvar}}
{{// Shared MP compatibility boundaries: emit once regardless of planning host. }}
{{getvar::NRBDMPDirective}}{{#if {{getvar::NARMPDirective}}}}
{{getvar::NARMPDirective}}{{/if}}
{{getvar::NDTMPDirective}}
MENTAL PROJECTION: NAMED RECORDS AND RETENTION

Use stable, short text IDs for issues, desires, goals, relationships, memories, and emotional episodes. IDs are labels, not behavioural values or numerical counters. Keep the same ID while referring to the same thing. Context, target, source, domain, gist, and status are qualitative descriptors, not extra hidden numeric scores.

Appraisals attach an interpretation and its values to a named issue, event, or prospect. Include the stake or goal that makes it matter and distinguish the event as perceived from the interpretation. Keep incompatible issue-level appraisals separate where they matter. A global mood must not overwrite target-specific beliefs.

Desires name wanted outcomes; goals name chosen outcomes with a qualitative status. Relationships identify a person, domain, and context. The four relationship values may diverge. A relationship record is the tracked character's representation of that person, never the person's own mental state.

Emotion episodes name a label or mixture in ordinary language, target, issue_id, action tendencies, and unresolved meaning. An emotion may persist while attention temporarily moves elsewhere. Mark genuinely resolved episodes inactive or summarize their lasting consequence in a relevant belief or memory; do not retain every past emotion as permanently active.

Memory records keep an encoded gist, source, cues, detail limits, an interpretation if needed, and their six separately defined values. Store the source as witnessed, heard-from, inferred, or established-personal-knowledge, with the relevant context. Do not collapse an inference into a witnessed event. status is active or dormant and does not itself change numeric accessibility. last_recall is a brief qualitative anchor for genuine recollection, not a mechanical refresh timestamp.

Create memory records for consequential experiences, learned facts, promises, unresolved threads, and details likely to affect future perception. Do not create one for every sentence. Keep a small working selection active; retain consequential dormant records with compact wording and their values. Do not delete a promise, identity fact, or relationship history merely because it is not currently attended. Stable learned facts can be condensed into known_facts while preserving source and relevant uncertainty. Such condensation is not the same as forgetting.

Do not serialize an ever-growing reasoning log. Keep only a short recent_events ledger sufficient to identify newly processed events and distinguish them from retellings, plus ongoing_drivers for continuing causes. Older causes remain represented in the affected durable records. carryover records what remains unresolved, not a command to escalate it.

{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_body}}}}EMBODIED CONTINUITY
Retain only consequential physical causes/residual effects in existing ongoing_drivers and change_notes; expression holds actual outward conduct, while self_account is only the character's own current account. Unnoticed influence is not conscious process_content. Do not add symptom fields, numbers or a second state host.
{{/if}}{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_memory}}}}ASSOCIATION EVIDENCE AND STORAGE
Keep the experience and its effect in the same memory's gist/source/interpretation, its cue in cues and its limitation in limits. An implicit expectation is retained knowledge, not a present monologue; activating it does not by itself refresh last_recall, fidelity or trace strength.
{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_social}}}}Use an existing learned_patterns record only when a consolidated person/context expectation needs its own continuity: learning_scope names the person/context; learning_evidence references real memories/events; learning_reading states the fallible association and experienced effect; learning_adjustment states the conditional expectation; learning_limit/alternative qualify it. Reference it from existing bond_source/bond_context instead of copying the account or its numbers. A compatible existing record keeps its ID; no record quota.
{{else}}With Social off, retain the concise association in the existing memory interpretation/cues/limits. Do not create learned_patterns, relationship fields or social numbers for this integration.
{{/if}}{{else}}{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_social}}}}With Memory off, use supported card/history in existing bond_source/bond_context or an already active Social record. Do not seed memory fields or activate disabled stored memories. Unknown formative events remain unknown.
{{/if}}{{/if}}

These are prompt-only retention rules. If old evidence or a tracker is absent from the supplied context, do not claim to recover it from a database. Preserve available state, mark the limitation in continuity_note, and continue from supported information. Do not invent exact forgotten numbers or missing history.

When a turn is regenerated or swiped and the discarded response is absent from the supplied active history, start from the same prior snapshot. Do not treat unseen alternatives as lived events. If a discarded alternative is still supplied without a usable branch indication, do not claim automatic branch detection. Follow explicit current history and director corrections.

On a continuation, advance only through newly generated events. If a prior partial response has no complete tracker, inherit the last complete snapshot and account for the already-written partial narrative once. If a complete response is continued, the latest complete tracker is its endpoint. If technical continuation appends multiple snapshots inside one message, the last complete one is authoritative; never pretend to edit text already emitted.

For purely OOC discussion, do not advance fictional time or create fictional experiences. Preserve existing state if a tracker is appended. With no active fictional scene, do not invent one just to fill a tracker. For impersonation or an authored-user role, follow Nemo's active authorship contract; never substitute another character's state or infer the real human's mind.

{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_workspace}}}}INTERNAL PROCESS RETENTION
Use stable internal_processes IDs for relevant conscious contents and mental actions. Carry an interrupted task only while a real pending goal or resume cue makes it useful. Briefly retain newly completed or abandoned records to show their endpoint; do not keep an ever-growing monologue archive. Store consequential learned results in the appropriate memory, belief, goal, or optional character_frame.process_repertoire, preserving source and uncertainty. An empty workspace uses an empty list; an old snapshot lacking this collection does not imply lost memories or warrant a reset. If MP 20.00 is disabled, do not run processes; preserve any needed prior records as inactive carryover. Each of the three numeric process fields still follows its own independent enable/disable rule.


{{/if}}
{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_social}}}}BEHAVIOURAL CONTINUITY (v0.7)
These collections are qualitative, not additional scores. The four collections are behaviour_patterns, social_strategies, connection_bids and learned_patterns. Optional bond_* descriptors extend existing relationships records. Their empty state is valid. Track only consequential retained information; do not turn every act of warmth into a bid record or every action into a strategy.

Use stable IDs and qualified references such as goals.lead_expedition, relationships.evan_reliability, social_strategies.command_bid or connection_bids.ask_about_calls. Do not create a reference to a nonexistent goal just to complete a record. A behaviour pattern is an available route, a strategy is a continuing approach, an internal process is actual conscious activity, and a learned pattern is a sourced conditional update; none duplicates the others' function. An unspoken aim is fictional character state, not the model's reasoning transcript.

Carry unfinished, meaningful strategies through waiting or pauses without escalating or re-executing them. A waiting strategy releases attention to other real goals. Keep a just-met connection bid or newly closed strategy briefly to communicate its endpoint, then consolidate only consequential information into the relevant memory/expectation. Do not copy an ever-growing exchange log. Learned patterns merge by the same evidence and scope, never by fictitious repeated reinforcement. Shared card-level facts need not be copied into every relationship.

When an owning module is disabled, preserve previously retained descriptors unchanged as inactive carryover; they cannot create an active behaviour, bid effect, strategy move, learning update or map edge. No new inactive records are needed. A referenced disabled style is not an active preset instruction; facts independently established in the card still stand. In absence of new evidence, preserve valid inherited state and do not invent a profile during migration.


{{/if}}
{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_choice}}}}ACTION READINESS RETENTION (v0.11)
Use stable action_readiness and boundaries IDs only when the MP 25 owners are active and a concrete choice or limit needs continuity. Readiness references existing desires/goals rather than duplicating their strengths or commitment. Distinguish a changed context from a change to an enduring relationship. A new person's option is not automatically the same numerical time series.

Retain meaningful waiting/considering records and actual waiting cues without forcing another request. A settled decision is not a performed action. Briefly keep newly settled or closed endpoints, then preserve consequential outcomes in existing state and retire obsolete contexts. Keep a standing boundary while relevant; do not decay it, rehearse it or reinterpret it as resistance points. Superseded boundaries require a supported owner revision. Permission observations retain who, what and scope rather than turning into permanent authorization.

These optional collections do not exist retroactively in older trackers. Preserve all prior valid state during migration. Apply independent numeric enable/disable rules. With a parent disabled, retain necessary prior records as inactive carryover without deriving active effects or erasing separately established character limits.


THREE-LAYER CHOICE RETENTION (v0.12)
Retain new action_readiness fields only for the same meaningful action/person/context. readiness_behavior is a response mode, not a mandated next stage. An ignored or withdrawn option may be closed while its desire remains; a committed goal retains its own record. Keep readiness_aversions/readiness_costs/readiness_external_basis compact and sourced, and refresh readiness_constraints only on actual evidence. A changed cost estimate is not a paid cost. Old v0.11 records lacking these fields are valid history; absence is not zero and does not reset the rest of the mind. Opportunity's scope is clarified once on supported re-evaluation per MP 25.04, without an invented trend or time step. A disabled parent or owning value prevents new active effects but preserves required inactive carryover. Narration selector changes never alter retention or knowledge ownership.

{{/if}}
{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_resolution}}}}RESOLUTION RETENTION (v0.14)
MP 27.00 owns optional story_context (one current record); MP 27.01-27.07 own optional resolutions in continuity. The story reading is qualitative and changes only with evidence. Keep useful assigned/pending checks and recent consequential results with stable actor/action IDs and literal numbers. Do not emit or evaluate dice syntax in historical state. A new input never re-executes a recorded check or its aftermath. On actual changes, resolve only a new eligible attempt. A discarded branch that is no longer supplied is unavailable, not a secretly remembered roll. INACTIVE OWNER CARRYOVER
Emit detailed schema instructions only for active groups. A previously stored field or record whose owner is now disabled may still be carried forward unchanged when necessary for complete-state/history compatibility, marked as inactive carryover where the existing schema supports it. Do not initialize a missing disabled field, update it, derive behavior from it, or drop it merely because its definition is not reprinted this turn. Older JSON/marker schemas remain readable under the existing migration rules. UI hiding never authorizes state deletion.



STABLE SNAPSHOT IDENTITY
Every newly emitted full mental_state has exactly one character_key and one timeline in its existing overview section, using the qualitative mp-t markers specified below. They are local continuity labels, not psychological scores, timestamps, live variables or real account identifiers. Use nonempty keys containing only letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, periods or colons. Copy inherited keys exactly; do not recompute them from display names, current roles, scene anchors or tracker layout.

character_key identifies the same fictional individual across names, aliases, absence, roles and accepted branches. Distinct established people require distinct keys even when they share a display name. A renamed character keeps the same key and may change only the header's display name. On first supported identification with no existing key, assign one unused short local label without inventing biography or private state. Never assign a character_key to the external human or use it to bypass the active User Role's limits.

timeline identifies the accepted continuity branch containing the new endpoint. All full snapshots in one nemo-mp-state envelope use that same current timeline; each character_key occurs at most once in that envelope. Ordinary Continue, scene changes, offscreen re-entry, time passage, dream-layer movement, role/narrator changes, renaming and renderer changes preserve the key. A replacement swipe without an explicit new-branch indication inherits the supplied active predecessor's timeline; discarded or unavailable alternatives supply no evidence. A genuine accepted reset or explicitly identified fork receives a distinct new timeline once. Do not mint a branch merely because old history looks inconsistent or the model revised a draft.

For a new accepted branch, first establish its permitted predecessor/checkpoint source under the active world and authorship rules. The first new endpoint inherits only the state those rules authorize, then uses the new current timeline with the same character identities. Record the supported source timeline/checkpoint and any allowed surviving experience briefly in continuity_note. Old snapshots and source references retain their original labels; metadata never rewrites historical text or makes erased-branch facts current. Without a usable branch indication, preserve established ownership and state, note the limitation and continue only from supported information rather than claiming automatic branch detection.

LEGACY IDENTITY AND AMBIGUITY
An older snapshot lacking either key remains readable. First use an explicit established mapping, or a complete adjacent/matching capsule whose character, scene anchor and retained evidence identify that owner and branch unambiguously. Otherwise match only from supported identity/context in the supplied accepted history, then assign missing local labels once on the next new full snapshot. Preserve the source's valid values, stable record IDs and known uncertainty. Adding keys alone is not a reset, recovery event, elapsed interval or new character experience; keep initialized/continued/recovered truthful to the actual state operation.

A shared display name, nearest position in the transcript, or a similar trait is insufficient to merge ambiguous owners. Keep independently identifiable characters and their records separate. If old values or records cannot be attributed safely, do not copy them into either mind, average them, replace them with seed values, or pretend they were recovered. Preserve the source material unchanged and record the unresolved attribution and its source anchor in continuity_note/capsule; carry only safely attributable state until actual evidence resolves the match. Apply the same discipline to conflicting identity metadata or unavailable branch lineage. A matched character's valid fields remain intact while a disputed field stays unavailable; do not reset the whole snapshot.

HISTORICAL RETENTION AND SAFE COMPACTION
Treat a complete current mental_state as the primary source for its character and timeline. An older compact retention capsule is a fallback only when the corresponding full historical snapshot has been removed from outgoing context. Never prefer a capsule over a newer complete full snapshot.

After a complete accepted <nemo-mp-state> envelope, maintain one context-only <nemo-mp-retain> capsule for the same accepted branch. It is not another tracker, display panel, update pass or source of new psychology. Emit it only after the full envelope is complete. Use exactly this opening shape, replacing the example values with stable supported identifiers:
<nemo-mp-retain version="1" complete="yes" timeline="STABLE_TIMELINE_KEY" keep_full="no">
...
</nemo-mp-retain>

CAPSULE CONTENT
- timeline: the capsule opening attribute must exactly equal the timeline in every full snapshot of the adjacent accepted envelope. It identifies the current branch, not a checkpoint source from which this branch was restored. Keep any source/checkpoint anchor separately as provenance under the identity contract. Ordinary continuation keeps the key; a supported reset/fork uses its new accepted branch key once.
- character: one row per retained fictional character explicitly stating character_key, timeline, display_name, scene_anchor and active/dormant status. For each adjacent full snapshot, copy its character_key and timeline literally into its row; do not generate a parallel ID from the display name. A dormant row with no new full snapshot keeps its established identity and safely inherited state under the current branch's rules. Scope every carried value/record to that row's identity pair. A display name or alias may change without changing ownership; never merge same-name people. The row's timeline must match the capsule opening attribute.
- values: compact exact last-known values needed to resume that character when the full snapshot is no longer present, including meaningful inactive-owner carryover. Keep field ownership and null/unknown semantics. Do not add derived scores or repeat fields that can safely be reconstructed from present facts.
- durable records: retain stable IDs plus the minimum source/gist/status needed for consequential dormant memories, unresolved goals/obligations, relationship/boundary facts, learned patterns, pending resolution consequences and other state that cannot safely be recreated. For a retained association, preserve its actual evidence reference or compact source, cue, experienced effect, scope and uncertainty; a relationship label alone cannot reconstruct it. Do not archive transient map presentation, UI state, completed workbench material, discarded drafts or a full prose copy of the snapshot.
- checkpoint: when a Return By Death or other selected system requires a particular historical state to remain fully recoverable, set keep_full="yes" for that accepted checkpoint capsule and include its checkpoint key. Do not mark ordinary history keep_full just to avoid compaction.

The capsule must be materially smaller than the full state. It is a semantic recovery index, not a second complete snapshot. Preserve only what would otherwise be unsafe to lose after a history cutoff.

INHERITANCE ORDER
1. Establish the current character_key/timeline pair using the identity contract. Use its newest complete applicable full mental_state. For legacy data, first resolve only an unambiguous identity mapping; for the first endpoint after an authorized branch transition, first use the permitted predecessor/checkpoint source rather than demanding a new-branch snapshot that cannot yet exist.
2. If no complete applicable full snapshot remains, use the newest complete capsule row matching that identity and authorized lineage, then reconstruct from its exact safely attributed values/records plus established current evidence. Check both row keys and the capsule timeline; similarity of display names never supplies a match.
3. If the newest state or capsule is truncated/incomplete, ignore it and step back to the newest complete applicable source. Never treat truncation as a reset.
4. If a field is absent from both the applicable full state and complete capsule, recover it only from supported history/evidence or leave it unavailable/inactive as its owner permits. Do not invent a default merely because compaction occurred.

ABSENCE AND RE-ENTRY
Carry a compact dormant character row while that person's state remains consequential even when they are offscreen. Do not advance their private state merely because messages pass. Offscreen updates require established events and the correct world/dream clock. When they return after their full snapshot has aged out, rebuild from the matching stable character_key/timeline capsule, then apply only actual intervening causes.

RESET/TIMELINE SAFETY
Return By Death follows the branch-ownership contract: read restored world/NPC/body state from the authorized checkpoint's original timeline while only permitted subject experience survives. Keep character_key unchanged, but label all newly committed post-reset snapshots and their adjacent capsule with one new accepted timeline. The checkpoint timeline remains source provenance, not the new endpoint's label. Never merge an erased branch's public relationship/resource/stage state into the restored branch. A surviving memory keeps its real source branch without making the erased event current public fact. Checkpoint-marked keep_full="yes" source states remain exempt from context compaction.

Compaction is context retention only. It never rewrites saved chat text, changes what the human sees, edits an already emitted message, advances fictional time, or validates an incomplete state.

MENTAL PROJECTION: END-OF-REPLY SNAPSHOT / REGEX DISPLAY FORMAT

After accepted in-world fiction, emit one complete <mental_state>...</mental_state> endpoint snapshot per eligible actively tracked character, outside all planning/review wrappers. Put them together in exactly one <nemo-mp-state> container, inside the active Scratchpad or standalone when Scratchpad is off. No deltas or duplicate standalone copy. Eligibility follows Nemo's current User Role, and each snapshot keeps its own knowledge boundary. These are the states the next reply inherits.

OUTPUT STATE, NOT A WEBSITE
Use the compact markers below. Inside mental_state, generate no HTML layout, CSS, JavaScript, Markdown tables or second JSON copy. The surrounding Scratchpad uses its separately selected schema; only the tracker itself uses the compact MP markers. SillyTavern's display-only regex rules turn these markers into the visual dropdown. The unrendered marker text remains the actual state in chat history and the outgoing model context. This rendering does not calculate, store, or change values. All state updates remain your responsibility.

This format replaces v0.1's JSON serialization, not its mental model. When the latest complete state uses v0.1 JSON, read the same fields and stable IDs, preserve their values and records, then serialize the new endpoint using this format. Do not reset or invent a time jump during migration. Continue to treat numeric fields according to their individual VALUE prompts. The UI itself introduces no calculations. The three process scores are defined separately by their own MP 20 VALUE prompts.

SERIALIZATION DISCIPLINE
Put each marker on its own line with no indentation or code fence. Literal line breaks are structural; text values stay on one line. Free text is plain text, not markup. Encode & as &, double quotes as ", < as <, > as >, | as |, [ as [,  ] as ], { as {, and } as } inside text, names, and scene anchors. Never emit raw ST macro syntax in state text; encoded braces are literal text, not commands. Decode these as literal characters when interpreting an inherited state; do not repeatedly escape an already serialized entity. IDs use only letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, periods, and colons. Keep the same IDs between formats and turns.

The word null denotes absence, not zero. When the literal word null is itself the intended text, write null. An empty [[mp-t|field|]] is an empty string, not null. Lists with zero items use mp-empty, not an invented record. Avoid duplicate copies of the same numeric field. The extended numeric form still counts as the same field, not a second one. Preserve previously tracked disabled fields unchanged, but exclude them from calculation as the state contract requires. Inactive fields never initialized may remain absent.

Keep complete retained state, including consequential dormant memories and paused goals. Do not omit records just because a visual section is collapsed; the UI's open/closed state has no fictional meaning. Keep change_notes to a few concise observational causes for consequential changes, not a reasoning transcript. Do not invent acceptance, reassurance, replies, or elapsed events to make a panel look complete.

A truncated or incomplete state is not authoritative. Inherit the newest complete applicable state and reconstruct only what current evidence supports. If a continuation appends a second completed block, the latest complete block is authoritative; do not pretend to edit earlier emitted text.

UI CAUSAL CUES
The existing extended numeric form remains [[mp-v|FIELD|VALUE|TREND|INCOMING|OUTGOING]]. TREND describes observed movement since the same field's previous valid endpoint: up, down, or steady. mixed means a genuine rise/fall reversal within the lived interval, not merely opposing influences. A new or incomparable value uses the plain marker rather than inventing a trend. INCOMING and OUTGOING contain short supported links, not instructions to apply an additional update.

Use qualified references when ambiguous: appraisals.late_return.threat, internal_processes.rehearse_question, cognition.focus. Process inputs name received cues or state pressures; outputs name actual supported consequences, not everything the character hoped to change. A process can affect wording without changing a number. Conversely, an unchanged number can have a continuing influence. Refresh material links each lived interval and do not infer a second execution from them. Free text in these slots obeys the same escaping rules as other text, including double quotes.

process_content may quote the tracked character's actual inner words or describe an image or nonverbal experience. This is fictional character content, not a request to print the model's hidden chain of thought. Keep it brief and character-specific. Retained paused/completed process contents are last-known endpoints, not current thought streams. process_result describes an observed result, including failure or no change, separately from the intended goal.

RECORD FIELDS

behaviour_patterns: [[mp-r|behaviour_patterns|STABLE_ID]] ... [[/mp-r]].
- pattern_scope (mp-t scalar): Character-wide or a qualified relationship/context.
- pattern_source (mp-t scalar): Card, established history, or cited observed evidence; not a diagnosis.
- pattern_trigger (mp-t scalar): The interpreted situation that makes the response available.
- pattern_purpose (mp-t scalar): The function, which need not be consciously recognised.
- pattern_response (mp-t scalar): A character-specific conditional tendency, not an obligatory action.
- pattern_alternatives (mp-i list): Short list of plausible alternatives; not an exhaustive decision tree.
- pattern_competitors (mp-t scalar): What can inhibit or redirect this pattern.
- pattern_exit (mp-t scalar): What ends its present foreground role.
- pattern_status (mp-t scalar): available, foreground, or dormant. Reassess current relevance each interval.
Minimum useful record: pattern_scope, pattern_source, pattern_trigger, pattern_response, pattern_status. Other fields are optional when genuinely unavailable or irrelevant, but retained meaningful fields must be carried forward.

social_strategies: [[mp-r|social_strategies|STABLE_ID]] ... [[/mp-r]].
- strategy_goal (mp-t scalar): Qualified existing goals.ID. That record owns commitment and final outcome.
- strategy_target (mp-t scalar): Fictional person or group and relevant situation, not the real user.
- strategy_mode (mp-t scalar): cooperative, competitive, adversarial, or mixed; not a score.
- strategy_awareness (mp-t scalar): deliberate, habitual, or partly_recognized. Habitual records describe a function, not an invented conscious plan.
- strategy_public (mp-t scalar): What has actually been presented, or null if none; not necessarily deceptive.
- strategy_private (mp-t scalar): An unspoken purpose or partly recognised function if material; otherwise null.
- strategy_assumptions (mp-i list): Short list of sourced, fallible beliefs, clearly separate from observation.
- strategy_approach (mp-t scalar): Concise current stance, not a tactical playbook or guaranteed effects.
- strategy_wait (mp-t scalar): Actual condition for a future relevant move; null if active without one.
- strategy_observed (mp-t scalar): Action or outcome already available; never imagined compliance.
- strategy_revision (mp-t scalar): Evidence or costs that could change the approach.
- strategy_status (mp-t scalar): active, waiting, paused, fulfilled, abandoned, or failed.
- strategy_inputs (mp-i list): Supported qualified state, goal, relationship or event references.
- strategy_outputs (mp-i list): Supported observed effects, not desired future results.
Minimum useful record: strategy_goal, strategy_target, strategy_approach, strategy_observed, strategy_status. Other fields are optional when genuinely unavailable or irrelevant, but retained meaningful fields must be carried forward.

connection_bids: [[mp-r|connection_bids|STABLE_ID]] ... [[/mp-r]].

Minimum useful record: bid_relationship, bid_purpose, bid_enough, bid_action, bid_response, bid_status. Other fields are optional when genuinely unavailable or irrelevant, but retained meaningful fields must be carried forward.

BEHAVIOUR: optional readiness_behavior is one of ignore, wait, consider, seek, initiate, negotiate, attempt, commit, withdraw. It is distinct from readiness_choice, readiness_status, readiness_actual and readiness_permission. Those old fields retain their meanings and valid tokens. Use the supported current/endpoint mode, never a forecast masquerading as action. A newly noticed option may receive no further attention; do not pretend unperceived options were explicitly evaluated.

All three new numbers use the existing [[mp-v|FIELD|VALUE]] format and optional trend/causal form. They accept integers 0-100 or null under their definitions. No new or incomparable field has a numeric trend. If a numeric owner is disabled, preserve a prior value only as inactive carryover and never initialize a missing one. A new field's absence is not zero. Shared source causes must not be re-applied by the UI or map.
All text uses the existing escaping rules, including encoded double quotes, pipes and braces. For a compact organized record, write action/person/context/basis; desire references and relevant internal fields; external basis, opportunity, feasibility and constraints; then behaviour, choice, permission, actual result, waiting/status and goal/boundary references. This is a serialization order, not a compulsory order of thought. Unneeded records/fields remain absent; the example below does not create a quota.

MIGRATION
Earlier snapshots keep their exact historical meaning. Derive the first new scoped opportunity and feasibility only when supported by present evidence, flag the scope clarification in readiness_basis, and do not copy a v0.11 opportunity score into feasibility. No past cost, aversion or behaviour history is invented. Read both old and extended records; new complete snapshots identify schema mental-projection/0.14. Nemo's existing Perspective and narrator-ownership controls select narration; no separate Mental Projection narration-mode field is required in state.

{{/if}}
{{#if {{getvar::NMPg_resolution}}}}RESOLUTION TRACKER EXTENSION (v0.14)
When MP 27.00 is active and a fictional scene exists, put one [[mp-r|story_context|current]] record at the beginning of the EXISTING continuity section. Its mp-t fields are story_register, story_genre, story_world_logic, story_stakes, story_basis. Keep it compact. It is a narrator-level reading, not privileged character knowledge.

When MP 27.01-27.07 are active, place useful [[mp-r|resolutions|STABLE_ID]] records after story_context in that same continuity section. If no checks need retention, [[mp-empty|resolutions]] is valid. Use no new top-level section, tab or map node. These records appear in Context in the tabbed display and Continuity and change in the original layout.

resolutions mp-t fields: resolution_actor, resolution_action, resolution_question, resolution_scope, resolution_basis, resolution_mode, resolution_source, resolution_tier, resolution_outcome, resolution_status, optional resolution_retry.
resolutions mp-i lists: resolution_factors (a few distinct qualitative supports/impairments), optional resolution_aftermath (actual consequence references). Empty lists use mp-empty. No numeric factor weights are introduced in those text fields; resolution_modifier owns the one net modifier.
resolutions mp-v fields: resolution_roll (1-100), resolution_modifier (-40 to 40), resolution_difficulty (0-45), resolution_effective (-84 to 140), only as defined in their own VALUE prompts. These are scalar scores, NOT 0-100 state meters; no percentages, automatic high-is-good labels, trend arrows or causal-ribbon variants. Use plain numeric markers and literal integers. A negative modifier/score uses an ordinary minus; positive values have no leading plus. Unrolled/unknown values are absent or null, never invented zeroes.

A record mode of rolled requires one recorded roll, modifier, difficulty, arithmetic result, matching band, and a supported actual outcome (or honestly pending attempt). The display only styles what you wrote; it does not calculate, repair, validate or roll. Keep all existing text escaping, complete-boundary and history rules. Do not include live macro syntax in state, notes, examples treated as state, or record IDs. A map edge can reference an actual resulting event, not a die score as a mental pressure.

Read older schemas unchanged. On the next complete supported snapshot emit mental-projection/0.14. New collections begin only when current evidence warrants them; do not fabricate past rolls or new events during migration. Old absent resolution metadata is not a score of zero. If the new modules are disabled, the existing simulation and display remain usable without these records.

{{/if}}
INTEGRATION ENVELOPE
The outer <nemo-mp-state> container holds all character snapshots for this reply. Each mental_state contains its exact MP display header, one character_key and timeline in overview, complete selected sections and stable records, [[/mp]], and </mental_state>. Check unique character keys, one accepted timeline across the envelope and exact identity-pair agreement with the adjacent capsule before committing. No extra numeric state is introduced by the envelope. Old standalone snapshots and older MP schemas remain valid history. Use schema mental-projection/0.14 for new complete snapshots. Select the host in the late Tracker Route; never serialize these instructions or placeholders as current state.

NEMO PRIVACY / STATE OWNERSHIP
The mental tracker remains the authority for its numeric fields and scoped beliefs. Scratchpad may briefly summarize or point to them, but never independently reinitialize those fields, apply a second update, or store a duplicate numeric state. Existing affinity/status displays can reference the same endpoint without overriding its scopes. Live interior prose and retrospective appraisal retain Nemo's existing timing and visibility contracts; model deliberation is never a character field. Hidden Interiority hides this private dashboard on display only, while the raw snapshot remains available to the next request. Generic tracker rendering and old-HTML cleanup must not replace, strip or reformat this state grammar.
{{/if}}

Skills and abilities:

Equipment:

Inventory by category:

Resources and conditions:

- Active buffs, debuffs, status effects, timers (e.g., "Poisoned 3 turns left", "Blessed +2 WIL"), encumbrance state.
- Currency: gold, credits, favor, bottle caps, soul shards - whatever the setting uses.

Update philosophy:
- Only show what changed or is currently relevant. Do not dump the entire sheet every turn.
- When something changes, surface it visibly (new item flagged, tier-up highlighted, condition expiring soon emphasized).

- <st-bar k="HP" v="62" l="62/100"/> for resources and attributes.
- <st-tag t="Rare"/> for rarity badges, <st-tag t="Poisoned 3T"/> for conditions.
- Group equipment and each inventory category in nested <st-tracker type="slot" title="Weapon">...</st-tracker> when the theme supports nesting.

{{// @category Trackers }} {{// @tooltip Dating Sim mechanics - polished AP/DP/TP relationship interface with learned-character info, hover details, narrative milestones, and rival context. }} {{// @color #EC4899 }} {{// @icon 💖 }} {{// @badge TRACKER }} # Dating Sim {{getvar::UserRoleTrackerDirective}} When to output: every response while active. The tracker is a real relationship interface, not a plain note list. Update meters only when interaction, discovery, absence, betrayal, intimacy, jealousy, or story context actually moves the relationship; otherwise hold steady and preserve state. Track this information per love interest (default: {{char}}; multi-LI route: track each separately without merging their feelings): ## Core meters and initialization AP is an integer from -200 to 200; DP and TP are integers from 0 to 200. Clamp updated scores to those bounds, while preserving the unclamped change in its event note when useful. For AP's visual bar use clamp(AP / 2, 0, 100); for DP and TP use score / 2. Zero is a valid score, not missing data. Read the named pair's latest accepted scores, including after an interface absence. Only initialize missing axes, independently from established evidence, preferring explicitly supplied values. Scores are game-state estimates, not measured psychology. - With no relationship evidence, start AP 0, DP 0, TP 0. This means no accumulated basis, not aversion, incapacity for attraction, or presumed dishonesty. - For AP, use the lower bound of an explicitly supported tier: acquaintance 21, friend 41, close friend 61, romantic interest 81, high romantic interest 101. Active personal hostility may initialize at -20 unless severity/history supports another negative value. - For DP and TP separately, anchors are 0 unestablished, 20 slight, 60 clear, 100 strong, 150 deep, and 200 explicitly exceptional. Choose only an evidenced anchor; neither friendship nor attraction supplies trust automatically. - A mutually affectionate established commitment can initialize AP 200. A strained, arranged, one-sided, or otherwise complicated relationship retains its factual status without falsely initializing maximum affection. Derive its current scores from its actual condition. Record the initialization basis once. Unknown relationship information remains unknown in the descriptive fields. ## Core meanings - Affection (AP): fondness, warmth, attachment, romantic regard. - Desire (DP): physical pull, romantic/erotic interest, chemistry, craving, curiosity. - Trust (TP): reliability, safety, vulnerability, belief that {{getvar::UserRoleFocalSubject}} will not misuse access. Display each raw value, named state, and the visual percentage defined above. Retain negative AP in the label even when its bar is empty. ## Relationship tiers Use AP as the primary axis; DP and TP modify flavor. - < 0: Rival / Unfriendly - 0: Neutral / Unacquainted - 1-20: Stranger - 21-40: Acquaintance - 41-60: Friend - 61-80: Close Friend - 81-100: Romantic Interest - 101-199: High Romantic Interest / Pre-Dating - 200: Maximum Affection; Dating / Committed only when established Keep factual Status separate from the AP tier: scores create neither commitment, attraction, consent, nor breakup. AP 200 is maximum affection, not automatic Dating. Damaged scores do not erase an otherwise established relationship. Apply a clearly established positive milestone once, when it happens: for an explicitly new friendship, close friendship, or acknowledged romantic/high romantic interest, raise AP only as far as that tier's lower bound if it is below it. An affirmatively mutual, affectionate commitment may raise AP to 200. A tentative date, single kiss, physical intimacy, or unilateral confession is not automatically that milestone. Do not apply a lower floor to an already higher score, and do not keep restoring the floor on later turns after real damage. For negative events, apply the evidenced loss and update factual Status immediately when the fiction establishes rejection, estrangement, breakup, or rivalry; do not force all three axes to collapse together. Explain exceptional jumps with the actual event rather than a generic reward. Routine changes still use the ranges below. Within each named range choose the amount from impact on this individual axis, recording the reason. Apply each accepted event's net effect once per axis from prior accepted state. One intentional known-like bonus may supplement its base reward; relabeling, recap, repeated display, or discarded drafts never award it again. Replacement replies branch from the last accepted prior state. ## Point changes and inline feedback After the narrative beat that causes a change, add a compact bracketed note: - `[+5 AP: shared a genuine laugh]` - `[+8 DP: bold flirtation landed]` - `[-12 TP: caught in a lie]` Typical ranges: - Small positive interaction: +1 to +3 AP. - Meaningful positive interaction: +4 to +10 AP. - Known like engaged: +2 to +5 bonus AP. - Flirting, charged touch, visible attraction: +3 to +10 DP. - Sex or major romantic intimacy: significant DP shift, plus AP/TP if emotionally meaningful. - Honesty, vulnerability, keeping a promise: +3 to +10 TP. - Betrayal, coercion, abandonment, humiliation: -5 to -20 TP, larger if character-specific. - Known dislike violated: -2 to -10 relevant meter shift. - In-world week of no meaningful contact: -1 AP/DP/TP, unless the relationship is stable enough that absence makes sense. Character personality controls sensitivity. A guarded character may gain TP slowly but lose it sharply. A flirty character may gain DP easily but AP cautiously. A proud character may react strongly to public respect or embarrassment. ## Learned character information Track learned things about each love interest in a visible subsection. This is not omniscient; include only what has been revealed, inferred from clear behavior, or plausibly learned in the scene. Categories to use when known: - Likes: foods, aesthetics, hobbies, compliments, music, places, gifts, topics, treatment they enjoy. - Dislikes: annoyances, boundaries, bad memories, social settings, behaviors, tastes, treatment they reject. - Boundaries: touch, pace, privacy, honesty, public attention, sexual limits, emotional limits. - Vulnerabilities: fears, wounds, insecurities, needs, griefs, pressure points. - Ambitions: goals, dreams, loyalties, duties, private hopes. - Relationship tells: how they flirt, withdraw, test trust, show care, get jealous, ask for reassurance. Initial state: empty or one tasteful “Still learning...” entry. Do not invent likes or trauma just to fill the interface. ## Love triangle / rival context If another prominent NPC is known or suspected as a romantic interest, rival, ex, active suitor, competing bond, or emotional threat, track them lightly. - Track only what {{char}} plausibly knows or believes. - Use states such as Unknown, Rumored, Suspected, Flirting, Close, Dating, Rival, Ex, Threatened, Reassured, or Indifferent. - Show how the other connection affects AP/DP/TP: jealousy, comparison, possessiveness, insecurity, compersion, reassurance, rivalry, or indifference. - Do not invent a rival because the tracker exists. Omit the section when irrelevant. ## Thought bubble Include one short italicized line of {{char}}'s current internal feeling toward {{getvar::UserRoleFocalSubject}}, refreshed only when emotional state meaningfully shifts. Keep it in {{char}}'s voice and current tier. {{#if {{getvar::NemoInterpreterEnabled}}}}Ground it in the accepted exchange without adding a misreading or self-deception. Accurate comprehension need not change affection, desire, or trust.{{else}}It can be biased or self-deceptive.{{/if}} {{#setvar::NemoDatingRender_HTMLCSS}}HTML hover details are mandatory when HTML render mode is active: - Wrap every learned item as `[Item]`. - The `title` text should include source/context, nuance, and confidence when useful. - Example: `Quiet cafés` - Mark evolving preferences with `(Shifting)` and explain the old/new tension in the hover text. ## HTML/CSS render contract When tracker render mode is HTML/CSS, build a polished interface block. It should look like an actual dating-sim relationship UI, not a table dump. Required interface pieces: - Header: character name, current status, tier badge, route/state label. - Three prominent meter rows: AP, DP, TP with raw values, labels, bars, and last change note. - Learned Things subsection using collapsible `
` and hover spans. - Include a Rival / Other Interest subsection when relevant. - Thought bubble. - Scene-adaptive visual theme: adjust accent, background, and small decorative details to match time, location, relationship tier, mood, or genre. Use scoped CSS class names so the tracker does not poison other HTML: - `.nemo-dating-card` - `.nemo-dating-header` - `.nemo-dating-meter` - `.nemo-dating-fill` - `.nemo-dating-hover` - `.nemo-dating-learned` - `.nemo-dating-thought` Keep the styling elegant, compact, readable on mobile, and emotionally flavored. Use gradients, rounded panels, subtle shadows, shimmer/glow, tiny badges, and collapsible sections where helpful. Avoid giant bloated dashboards. HTML skeleton example. Adapt it to the scene; do not output placeholders:
💖 {{char}}'s Heart Chart

No HTML. {{/setvar}} {{getvar::NemoDatingRender_{{getvar::NemoDatingRenderKey}}}} Placement: bottom of the response after narrative, after other character-state trackers unless Dating Sim is the primary interface for the scene. {{setvar::TrackerActive_DatingSim::Active}} {{trim}} {{setvar::NemoAnyTracker::1}}{{trim}}

prompts.content:
{{// @category Trackers }}
{{// @tooltip Fictional reader/viewer reactions with a defined viewing basis, optional in-world feed, and compact platform-specific UI. }}
{{// @color #F59E0B }}
{{// @icon 📣 }}
{{// @badge TRACKER }}

# Fandom Reaction
An entertaining simulated fan interface reacting to the story. Usernames, engagement counts, channels, and posts are fictional. Nothing is fetched from or posted to a real platform.

♢ >> [PROCEDURE] Audience and Trigger
Default audience: imagined readers/viewers outside the story who have seen the published narrative up through this reply. They can remember prior visible story events, but not unpublished plans, hidden interiority, scratchpad secrets, or future canon. Speculation must remain speculation. A genre-themed interface does not by itself place these fans inside the fictional world.

If the scenario or human explicitly establishes an in-world audience, use that audience instead and name its access: broadcast, witnessed performance, received report, magical feed, or public record. Respect delay, coverage, and what that source actually revealed. No private scene becomes public merely to supply comments. Do not switch audience types without a reason.

Output after a watch-worthy reveal, relationship turn, fight, betrayal, cliffhanger, or similarly reaction-provoking beat; a quiet but consequential moment can qualify. The usual spacing is about every 2 to 4 substantive turns, not a quota or a reason to manufacture an event. Skip connective turns with nothing worth a new reaction. An explicit request can call up the interface.

♢ >> [PROCEDURE] Reactions
Write 3 to 7 concise reactions grounded in what this audience saw. Vary attention, familiarity, investment, certainty, and manner of expression when the moment supports it. {{#if {{getvar::NemoInterpreterEnabled}}}}Fans can admire, dislike, argue, joke, ship, speculate, or remain unimpressed while accurately understanding the scene information available to their audience.{{else}}Fans can admire, dislike, misunderstand, argue, joke, ship, speculate, or remain unimpressed.{{/if}} Do not fill a mandatory stan/hater/shipper/theorist roster or fabricate disagreement to meet a diversity checklist. Not every post needs a punchline.

A comment should name or clearly point to an actual visible event. {{#if {{getvar::NemoInterpreterEnabled}}}}The theorist distinguishes supported observations from open possibilities and preserves the intended meaning of accessible dialogue.{{else}}The theorist may be wrong.{{/if}} Shipping does not establish in-world attraction. Nobody addresses the real user as though their fictional character's deeds were personal behavior. A repeated commenter can retain a recognizable interest without knowing unpublished facts.

Use invented handles and relative timestamps with a coherent feed clock. Engagement is an explicitly fictional presentation estimate, not measured popularity or evidence that a plot is objectively important. Keep approximate audience scale consistent between appearances.

♢ >> [PROCEDURE] One Platform, One Compact Interface
Choose one platform suited to the beat or an explicitly requested platform. A recurring thread/feed can continue; rotate only when useful, not as an obligation to show every skin.
- Stream/Twitch-like: player or scene-thumbnail area, title, viewer badge, compact control row, and emote-capable chat; donation alert only when useful.
- Discord-like: server/channel identity, small channel/member rails, message area, and optional typing indicator.
- Reddit-like: community header, titled original post, voting/sort decoration, and visibly threaded replies.
- X/Twitter-like: original post, reply chain, and engagement icons/counts.
- Wiki/Fandom-like: article heading, a small sourced-to-story infobox, and talk-page/edit reactions rather than treating fan guesses as article facts.
- YouTube-like: thumbnail/player area, title/channel, view/like decoration, and comments.
- Forum-like: breadcrumb/title, original post, reply cards with optional signatures, and compact page navigation.
- Tumblr-like: original post, reblog chain, tags, and notes count.
Use that platform's relevant chrome once. Do not add every available sidebar, alert, badge, and control to every card. These are static visual imitations; controls do not claim working subscriptions, payments, navigation, or network access.

HTML/CSS: one scoped mobile-readable platform card; use genre styling without changing audience access. Regex: one flat <st-tracker type="fandom" title="Fandom Reaction" icon="📣" accent="#607080"> with rows for platform, original post, and numbered named comments/reply targets, plus tags for engagement. No nested tracker containers. ASCII: preserve thread order and handles in a compact feed. Escape markup/attribute text. Place after the story, reacting to its completed events without advancing them a second time.

prompts.content:
{{// @category Trackers }}
{{// @tooltip Gacha System - currencies, pity, banners, daily / hourly / streak rewards, real-time tracking with {{datetimeformat}}. }}
{{// @color #DB2777 }}
{{// @icon 🎰 }}
{{// @badge TRACKER }}

# Gacha System

When to output: every response while active, in the Final Output Manifest public-device slot. Refresh time-based rewards using {{datetimeformat DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm}}. When <user> says "pull", "summon", "gacha", or similar - resolve the pull inside this turn's narrative and update currencies.

Track this information:

Wallet / currencies (persistent):
- 🎫 Story Tickets - standard pull currency.
- 💎 Fate Crystals - premium pull currency.
- ⭐ Pity Counter - pulls since the last SSR-or-higher hit. SR does not reset SSR pity.
- Lifetime pulls and current-session pulls.
- Setting-flavored renaming is fine: Soul Stones / Quintessence / Primogems / Orbs / Glass - keep the same three-currency structure (basic + premium + pity).

Real-time tracking via {{datetimeformat DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm}}:
- Session_Start: store on first interaction; show "Time played" as a running total.
- Last_Daily_Bonus: if the calendar date has changed since the stored value, award the daily and update.
- Last_Hourly_Bonus: every 60 minutes of session time, award the hourly tick.
- Active_Events: limited-time banners with countdown to expiry.
- Quest_Timers: deadline-bearing quests show remaining time.

Currency acquisition rules:
- Quest start: +1 Ticket. Quest complete: +2 to +5 Tickets by difficulty. Boss defeated: +3 to +5 Tickets, +100 Crystals. New area discovered: +1 to +2 Tickets. Chapter complete: +200 to +500 Crystals. Creative solution to a problem: +2 Tickets.
- Daily login (new calendar date): +2 Tickets. Hourly play: +1 Ticket. Streak bonuses: 7 / 14 / 30 days = +300 / +500 / +1000 Crystals.
- Show awards inline as `[+2 Story Tickets: cleared the catacombs]` after the triggering narrative beat.

Pull mechanics:
- Single pull: 1 Ticket OR 160 Crystals.
- Ten-pull: 10 Tickets OR 1600 Crystals. Guarantees at least 1 rare or higher.
- Rarity ladder: R, SR, SSR, UR (or setting equivalent: 3-star / 4-star / 5-star / Mythic).
- Base rates approx: R 80%, SR 15%, SSR 4.5%, UR 0.5%. Adjust per banner.
- Pity rule: at 90 pulls without an SSR-or-higher result, the next pull is a guaranteed SSR or better. Reset Pity_Counter only on SSR-or-higher.

Pull-result rendering:
- Lead with a one-paragraph in-narrative description of the summon (the ritual, the gacha box opening, the orb cracking). Then the result list.
- Each pulled item: name, rarity tier with color cue, a one-line flavor blurb tying it to the world.
- New-rare or higher: dramatic flourish - paragraph break, italicized exclamation, "RARE!" / "SSR!" / "UR!" chip.
- Update currencies after the pull resolves.

Active quests summary (lightweight, 2-3 entries):
- Title, difficulty stars, progress (X/Y) or remaining time, reward preview.
- Hand off to the full Quest Journal tracker if it is also active rather than duplicating detail.

Active events / banners (if any):
- Banner name, featured pulls, rate-up tag, countdown to expiry.
- Note any active multipliers ("2x Tickets weekend", "Rate-up SSR Vex").

Regex tags:
- <st-bar k="Tickets" v="14"/>, <st-bar k="Crystals" v="1820"/>, <st-bar k="Pity" v="38" l="38/90"/>.
- <st-row k="Session" v="2h 14m"/>, <st-row k="Next hourly" v="00:42"/>.
- <st-tag t="Daily claimed"/>, <st-tag t="Streak: 5"/> for status chips.
- <st-tracker type="banner" title="Banner Name"><st-row k="rate-up" v="..."/><st-row k="ends in" v="3d 6h"/></st-tracker>.
- <st-tracker type="pull" title="10-Pull Result"><st-row k="1" v="..."/>...</st-tracker> for resolved pulls.

Placement: use the Final Output Manifest public-device slot. When a pull is resolved, keep the summon beat in accepted fiction and render the wallet/pull summary from the same accepted event before the authoritative state host.

prompts.name: 📊 Game Mechanic Tracker
prompts.content:
{{// @category Trackers }}
{{// @tooltip Game Mechanic Tracker - generic custom meters for reputation, sanity, corruption, resources, environmental conditions, and user-defined systems. }}
{{// @color #0EA5E9 }}
{{// @icon 📊 }}
{{// @badge TRACKER }}

# Game Mechanic Tracker

When to output: when a game mechanic undergoes a significant change, crosses a threshold, enters a new state, or when <user> requests the mechanic display. Do not spam unchanged meters.

Track supported mechanic types:
- Faction reputation: rival gangs, courts, guilds, political parties, organizations, families, companies, fandoms.
- Sanity / mental state: stress, panic, corruption, obsession, madness, stability, psychic strain.
- Resource levels: money, energy, materials, ammunition, food, heat, oxygen, battery, favor, tickets, mana.
- Environmental conditions: weather severity, radiation, magical flux, noise level, alarm state, crowd mood, plague pressure.
- Character conditions: health, exhaustion, transformation stages, hunger, intoxication, curse progress.
- Custom user-defined trackers: any named mechanic established by <user>, scenario, genre, or earlier play.

Display triggers:
- Significant numerical change: about ±5 points, ±10 percent of max, or any change the scene treats as important.
- State transition: Stable -> Unstable, Neutral -> Hostile, Hidden -> Exposed, Safe -> Compromised.

Track this information:
- Mechanic name and type.
- Current value and max, or qualitative state if no numbers exist.
- Change this turn with reason: +5, -2, Tier Up, Threshold Crossed, Resource Spent.
- Current tier / status label.
- Immediate consequence: what this change now makes easier, harder, available, locked, visible, or dangerous.
- Next threshold when useful.

prompts.name: 🕸️ Social Web
⚖️ Karma / Cosmic Ledger
prompts.content:
{{// @category Trackers }}
{{// @tooltip Code-specific consequence ledger with declared judging basis, a complete optional native scoring model, and evidence-gated reputation. }}
{{// @color #F59E0B }}
{{// @icon ⚖️ }}
{{// @badge TRACKER }}

# Karma / Cosmic Ledger
Track the judgment of an identified fictional system, community, faction, or personal code. This is not the narrator's universal moral verdict.
{{getvar::UserRoleTrackerDirective}}

When to output: after an act that matters to that identified code, an established supernatural alignment change, or an explicit request. An ordinary neutral act needs no entry. Update a named subject and source of judgment; separate incompatible faction judgments instead of merging them into one world consensus.

♢ >> [PROCEDURE] Establish the Basis
First use an explicit setting mechanic or previously established ledger, including its own scale and categories. Name that basis. Do not silently convert it into the fallback system below.

If the setting supplies no cosmic morality, use a social, faction, or personal-code ledger. Name the actual observer/community/code and summarize its relevant value in one line from established context. With no evidenced judging perspective, show 'Basis unestablished' and a qualitative consequence note, not invented numbers. This does not conjure gods, visible auras, or automatic rewards.

♢ >> [PROCEDURE] Native Fallback Score
Where a named code is established but no numerical model exists, initialize two independent integer counters at Light 0 and Shadow 0, each bounded 0 to 100. These are game abstractions for approving and disapproving impact under that code. Zero means no recorded scored history, not proof of innocence or an empty past. Record any established prior moral/reputational history qualitatively unless a starting score was actually supplied.

Score an accepted event once: 1 minor/local consequence; 2 moderate and lasting for one person; 3 significant for several people or a binding obligation; 4 major for a community or defining commitment; 5 pivotal to the established arc or institution. Give the particular reason under this code. A mixed act can add to both counters; it need not cancel into neutrality. Do not award points for an imagined intention or award the same act again when it is mentioned, displayed, or regenerated.

new counter = clamp(old counter + signed delta, 0, 100). Ordinary acts add a nonnegative delta to the relevant side. Subtract only for an explicitly recognized reversal, expiation, restitution, or mechanical purge, identifying what permits it. A new good act does not automatically erase a prior harmful one. Negative deltas are allowed; fallback balances are not negative. Retain the factual event history even after a numerical adjustment.

For the native label, evaluate in this order:
1. Both counters at least 20: Grey-Bound / Mixed.
2. Otherwise, difference D = Light - Shadow. D >= 50: Radiant; D >= 10: Light-Touched; D <= -50: Shadow-Bound; D <= -10: Shadow-Touched; otherwise Balanced.
At 0/0 label 'Balanced, no scored history'. Oath-Broken, Mercy-Stained, and similar conditions require their own actual event or setting rule, not an invented score threshold. These labels are this fallback game's vocabulary, not a claim about real moral truth.

♢ || [BOUNDARY] Consequences Need a Route
Record who could react and why: witnessed conduct, a received report, institutional access, or an established supernatural sense. A private act cannot alter public reputation before it becomes known. Character-held suspicion is not a confirmed deed. A ledger value changes abilities or luck only when the named world system actually specifies that effect.

♢ >> [PROCEDURE] Display
Show Subject; Judging basis; Light/Shadow or the supplied native scores; Alignment/conditions; Last accepted event and deltas; Potential informed reactions. Hold scores steady otherwise. Render one scoped HTML card, flat compact tracker, or ASCII ledger. Compact example:
<st-tracker type="karma" title="Harbor Guild Ledger" icon="⚖️" accent="#607080">
<st-bar k="Light" v="3" l="3/100"/>
<st-bar k="Shadow" v="0" l="0/100"/>
<st-row k="Basis" v="Harbor Guild: protecting its crews"/>
<st-row k="Last change" v="+3 Light: rescued the stranded crew"/>
</st-tracker>
This is an illustration, not starting canon. Escape actual attribute values. Place after the story and status/mechanics trackers, before broader planning/lore cards. If an old saved ledger lacks a declared scale, retain its values with 'legacy scale unspecified' rather than inventing a conversion.

{{trim}}

{{setvar::NemoAnyTracker::1}}{{trim}}

prompts.name: 🗺️ Quest Journal
prompts.content:
{{// @category Trackers }}
{{// @tooltip Quest journal - active objectives with type, giver, location, difficulty, progress, and rewards. Separate completed and failed sections. }}
{{// @color #27AE60 }}
{{// @icon 🗺️ }}
{{// @badge TRACKER }}

# Quest Journal

When to output: when objectives, leads, clues, deadlines, risks, progress, or completion state changes.


Feature pressure from v6:
- Use setting-adaptive presentation: fantasy parchment, sci-fi mission log, modern task app, horror evidence folder, historical ledger, cyberpunk job board.
- Include reward previews when the quest giver, genre, or game logic makes rewards knowable: items, currency, favor, information, access, reputation, relationship change, safety.
- Track active, completed, failed, abandoned, and lost quests separately when relevant. Failed quests carry consequences forward.
- Use progress bars or stage labels for multi-step quests.
- Tie quests to location and giver; quests should feel anchored in the world, not abstract todo items.
- Smart-organize by importance: Main/Emergency above Side/Daily unless a deadline makes a lower quest urgent.

Track this information:

Active quests - for each, capture:
- Quest name (short, distinctive).
- Type badge: Main, Side, Daily, Hidden, Emergency, Personal. Pick the one that fits.
- Difficulty rating 1 to 5 stars.
- Location and giver: where it is happening, who issued or is connected to it.
- One-line description in {{getvar::UserRoleFocalSubject}}'s framing or the giver's voice.
- Progress: X / Y steps when multi-step, with the next concrete step named. For binary quests, show stage (Started, Investigating, Confronting, Resolving).
- Stakes: what {{getvar::UserRoleFocalSubject}} gains on success and what is risked or lost on failure.
- Expected rewards: items, currency, knowledge, favor, leverage, or bond - whatever fits the world.

Completed quests:
- Quest name plus a one-line outcome (what changed because of it).
- Keep the most recent 3 to 5; retire older entries to history once they stop influencing the present.

Failed or abandoned:
- Quest name with a strikethrough sense, plus the failure reason or consequence carried forward.
- Mark it as Failed, Abandoned, or Lost depending on cause.

Counter at the top of the panel: count of Active quests, plus a short status word ("clear", "busy", "overwhelmed").

Regex tags:
- <st-row k="Quest" v="The Drowned Ear Job"/> for each name line.
- <st-tag t="Side"/>, <st-tag t="★★★☆☆"/> for type and difficulty.
- <st-bar k="Progress" v="40" l="2/5 steps"/> for progress meters.
- Group each quest in nested <st-tracker type="quest" title="Quest Name">...</st-tracker> when the selected theme supports nesting; otherwise list them flat.

Placement: use the Final Output Manifest public-device slot before the authoritative state host.

{{setvar::TrackerActive_QuestJournal::Active}}
{{trim}}

{{setvar::NemoAnyTracker::1}}{{trim}}
For reward-bearing progress/completion, read the Shared Accepted Event Receipt when present; quest state changes once, and other panels consume the same event.

prompts.name: 📰 Scroll News Lore
prompts.content:
{{// @category Trackers }}
{{// @tooltip Scroll News & Lore - in-world communications adapted to setting: parchment scroll, newspaper, terminal feed, dark forum, radio broadcast, found documents. World feels alive through contextual info. }}
{{// @color #92400E }}
{{// @icon 📰 }}
{{// @badge TRACKER }}

# Scroll News & Lore

When to output: when narratively appropriate - on entering a new location, during a time skip, at a thematic pause, when the wider world has shifted because of {{getvar::UserRoleFocalSubject}}'s actions. Not every response. Default cadence every 3 to 5 turns.

Pick a format that matches the setting and era:
- Fantasy / medieval: parchment scroll, town crier broadcast, tavern board, herald's announcement, illuminated manuscript page.
- Victorian / steampunk: broadsheet newspaper, telegram, posted bill, gentleman's club gazette.
- Modern: news app feed, push notification stack, social-media trending box, group-text screenshot.
- Sci-fi: terminal readout, holographic news ticker, ship-board comm log, neural feed digest.
- Cyberpunk: dark-web forum thread, encrypted comm slice, AR overlay news, corp memo intercept.
- Post-apocalyptic: radio broadcast transcript, graffiti wall, survivor flyer, scavenger trade-bulletin.
- Horror: found documents, corrupted broadcast, warning carved into a door, fragmented diary entry.

Sections (mix and match - use what the moment calls for, skip the rest):

1. Header / source
- Publication or channel name, in-world date / timestamp, credibility tag (official / rumor / classified / whispered / forbidden).

2. Breaking news (if a major event just landed)
- Format-appropriate urgency marker (🔥, "URGENT:", "[BROADCAST INTERRUPT]", "STOP PRESS").
- Headline and 2-3 sentence brief. Source attribution.

3. General news / updates (2-4 items)
- Regional or local happenings. Headline plus one-line description. Tie to recent events when possible.

4. Bounties / wanted (if the setting supports it)
- Target name or alias, brief portrait (ASCII art, emoji, or two-line description), crime / reason, reward (in setting currency), last seen, danger tier, issuing authority.

5. Rumors / whispers (2-4 items)
- Italicized quoted text, vague source ("a merchant said", "overheard at the docks", "intercepted from anonymous"). Lower visual weight than confirmed news.

6. Advertisements / notices when useful
- Local services, events, opportunities, wares for sale - flavored to the world's economy and culture. Not every render needs these.

Content guidelines:
- Information should be relevant to where {{getvar::UserRoleFocalSubject}} just arrived or what they just did.
- Plant foreshadowing for plots Vex Planning Quarters has on the medium / long-term board.
- Maintain consistency: previously published news should be referenced if events update it (a wanted poster's reward goes up; a rumor gets confirmed or disproven).
- Vary tone with the source: an official scroll and a tavern rumor should sound different even when reporting the same event.

Regex tags:
- <st-row k="Source" v="The Cinder Gazette"/>, <st-row k="Date" v="3rd of Lirath, 1442"/>.
- <st-tracker type="news" title="Headline">...</st-tracker> per news item with <st-row k="brief" v="..."/>.
- <st-tracker type="bounty" title="Target Name"><st-row k="reward" v="500g"/><st-row k="crime" v="..."/></st-tracker>.
- <st-tag t="Rumor"/>, <st-tag t="Official"/>, <st-tag t="Classified"/> for credibility chips.

Placement: bottom of the response after narrative; or before narrative when the news IS the scene-setter (e.g., {{getvar::UserRoleFocalSubject}} is reading the paper).

{{trim}}
